items.description: `enabled: true` with empty `sources` is deny-all.

Customer-configurable deployment sources. Every deploy classifies to exactly one. JSON schema in `packages/deployment-policy/schemas/body.ts` enumerates exactly these values. - `'git'` — git provider webhook. - `'cli'` — Vercel CLI (legacy classic-token CLI and SIWV CLI both). - `'rest-api'` — direct user/team-token REST upload. Does NOT cover deploy hooks, Marketplace integrations, or first-party app tokens. - `'deploy-hook'` — project deploy-hook URL. The URL is the credential. - `'integration'` — third-party Marketplace actor: Marketplace integration token, user-delegated OAuth from a Marketplace app, or an unrecognized third-party Vercel App. First-party Vercel Apps are never `'integration'`. - `'v0'` — the v0 product surface (entitlement-gated). v0 deploys through the CLI under the hood, but classifies as its own source so a team can allow or deny v0 independently of `'cli'`. First-party Vercel apps (Toolbar, etc.) classify as `'first-party'` — see `ClassifiedSource` in `./checks`. They're not in this union because they aren't customer-configurable; they bypass `checkDeploymentSources` entirely. v0 is intentionally NOT among them: like the CLI, it's a real product surface and is policy-controllable.
`enabled: true` with empty `sources` is deny-all.

oneOf.description: Allowlist entry for GitHub and Bitbucket, whose repos are identified by a flat `org`/`repo` (Bitbucket's workspace/owner maps to `org`, its repo slug to `repo`). Omit `repo` to match any repo in the org. Org is matched case-insensitively.

Allowlist entry for GitLab, which uses nested groups rather than a flat org/repo. `namespace` is the full group path (e.g. `group` or `group/subgroup`); `project` is the leaf project name. Omit `project` to match any project under the namespace. Namespace is matched case-insensitively.

isEnvVar.description: When there was only one bypass, it was automatically set as an env var on deployments. With multiple bypasses, there is always one bypass that is selected as the default, and gets set as an env var on deployments. As this is a new field, undefined means that the bypass is the env var. If there are any automation bypasses, exactly one must be the env var.

note.description: Optional note about the bypass to be displayed in the UI

rollbackDescription.description: Description of why a project was rolled back, and by whom. Note that lastAliasRequest contains the from/to details of the rollback.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the rollback was requested.

description.description: User-supplied explanation of why they rolled back the project. Limited to 250 characters.

userId.description: The user who rolled back the project.

username.description: The username of the user who rolled back the project.

rollingRelease.description: Project-level rolling release configuration that defines how deployments should be gradually rolled out

canaryResponseHeader.description: Whether the request served by a canary deployment should return a header indicating a canary was served. Defaults to `false` when omitted.

gate.description: Automated gating configuration. Omitted (the default) means no gating is configured, which is equivalent to `enabled: false`.

action.description: What to do when the gate trips: pause the rollout, or roll it back.

checks.description: The checks to evaluate. An empty array means nothing is evaluated.

items.description: The checks to evaluate. An empty array means nothing is evaluated.

excludePaths.description: Request paths to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Matched exactly against the request path with any query string removed; no prefix or glob matching. Defaults to `[]` when omitted.

excludeStatusCodes.description: Response status codes to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Defaults to `[]` when omitted.

ingestWatermarkSeconds.description: Seconds of ingest lag to allow for: the query's upper bound is `now() - this value`, so the check never reads a window that is still filling. Defaults to `30` when omitted.

minSampleSize.description: Minimum number of requests required in the window before the check can fail. Below this, the check is inconclusive rather than failing, so low-traffic stages don't gate on noise. Defaults to `100` when omitted.

dryRun.description: When true, a tripped gate is only reported — {@link action} is not taken.

enabled.description: Whether automated gating is enabled for this project's rollouts.

failureThreshold.description: How many failing evaluations within {@link windowSize} trip the gate. Defaults to `3` when omitted.

windowSize.description: How many of the most recent evaluations {@link failureThreshold} is counted against. Defaults to `5` when omitted.

stages.description: An array of all the stages required during a deployment release. Each stage defines a target percentage and advancement rules. The final stage must always have targetPercentage: 100.

items.description: An array of all the stages required during a deployment release. Each stage defines a target percentage and advancement rules. The final stage must always have targetPercentage: 100.

duration.description: Duration in minutes for automatic advancement to the next stage

linearShift.description: Whether to linearly shift traffic over the duration of this stage

requireApproval.description: Whether or not this stage requires manual approval to proceed

targetPercentage.description: The percentage of traffic to serve to the canary deployment (0-100)

target.description: The environment that the release targets, currently only supports production. Adding in case we want to configure with alias groups or custom environments.

pageIntegrityEnabled.description: Whether Page Integrity is enabled for this project. Used by the metadata service to gate DynamoDB lookups against the page-integrity-inventory table.

framework.description: Framework slug, when the service has one (omitted otherwise).

runtime.description: Generic runtime, e.g. 'node' | 'python' | 'go' | 'ruby' | 'rust' (Service.runtime). Omitted for static builds.

serviceType.description: Service kind (Service.type). Omitted for schemas that do not define one.

dataReceivedAt.description: When the first free (not Speed Insights Plus) production data point was observed, in ms. Set once by subscriber-analytics-events; projects that already had data before this field shipped get it backfilled on their next batch, so it reads "first free data point observed", not necessarily "first ever".

pattern.description: The pattern to match against branch names

type.description: The type of matching to perform

previewCommentsEnabled.description: Whether or not preview comments are enabled for the deployment

userId.description: Present for user creators; omitted for app/integration/system creators.

destination.description: Which tracing destination this rule applies to. `internal` is the hidden Vercel production-tracing drain (internal delivery); `external` is any customer-configured drain. Derived from the owning drain's delivery type when project tracing is computed; absent on configs persisted before this field existed.

enableVercelCiSameRepository.description: Allow same-team Vercel CI access to preview deployments built from the CI run's repository, using the deployment source rather than the current project repository link. Defaults to enabled when not stored; omitted or null Trusted Sources updates preserve the stored value.

oneOf.description: The target envs on the current project that may be accessed.

slugs.description: System environment slugs (`production`, `preview`) and/or custom environment slugs defined on the referenced project.

customAllow.description: Optional overrides for the default same-env-by-slug matching. Provide explicit rules to allow cross-env access or presets.

items.description: Optional overrides for the default same-env-by-slug matching. Provide explicit rules to allow cross-env access or presets.

bypassThrottleUntil.description: Timestamp until which throttling is bypassed (project pays list rates for overage).

exceededAllowanceUntil.description: Timestamp until which the project has exceeded its CDN allowance.

kind.description: Billing mode. Always 'flat' for flat-rate projects.

teamThrottled.description: Synced from `team.billing.usageStatus.throttled`. When `true`, the team has throttled all of its projects regardless of `throttled`. The effective throttle the CDN enforces is `throttled || teamThrottled`.

throttled.description: Per-project throttle, set explicitly for this project (e.g. via the per-project Flat Rate CDN endpoint).

config.description: projectIds are added when the config is uploaded to s3 deployment assets.

development.description: Development configuration for the default application.

fallback.description: Fallback for local development, could point to any environment. This is required for the default app. This value is used as the fallback for child apps as well if they do not have a fallback. If passing a string, include the protocol (optional), host (required) and port (optional). For example: `https://this.ismyhost:8080`. If omitted, the protocol defaults to HTTPS. If omitted, the port defaults to `80` for HTTP and `443` for HTTPS. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.

task.description: The task to run when starting the development server. Should reference a script in the package.json of the application. The default value is "dev". See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.

packageName.description: The name used to run the application, e.g. the `name` field in the `package.json`. This is used by the local proxy to map the application config to the locally running app. This is only necessary when the application name does not match the `name` used in `package.json`. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/configuration#application-naming.

assetPrefix.description: The name of the asset prefix to use instead of the auto-generated name. The asset prefix is used to prefix all paths to static assets, such as JS, CSS, or images that are served by a specific application. It is necessary to ensure there are no conflicts with other applications on the same domain. An auto-generated asset prefix of the form `vc-ap-<hash>` is used when this field is not provided. When this field is provided, `/${assetPrefix}/:path*` must also be added to the list of paths in the `routing` field. Changing the asset prefix after a microfrontend application has already been deployed is not a forwards and backwards compatible change, and the asset prefix should be added to the `routing` field and deployed before setting the `assetPrefix` field. The default value is the auto-generated asset prefix of the form `vc-ap-<hash>`. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#asset-prefix.

fallback.description: Fallback for local development, could point to any environment. If not provided for child apps, the fallback of the default app will be used. If passing a string, include the protocol (optional), host (required) and port (optional). For example: `https://this.ismyhost:8080`. If omitted, the protocol defaults to HTTPS. If omitted, the port defaults to `80` for HTTP and `443` for HTTPS. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.

See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/configuration#application-naming.

routing.description: Groups of path expressions that are routed to this application. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing.

items.description: Groups of path expressions that are routed to this application. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing.

flag.description: The name of the feature flag that controls routing for this group of paths. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#routing-changes-safely-with-flags.

paths.description: A list of path expressions that are routed to this application. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#supported-path-expressions.

options.description: Optional configuration options for the microfrontend.

disableOverrides.description: If you want to disable the overrides for the site. For example, if you are managing rewrites between applications externally, you may wish to disable the overrides on the toolbar as they will have no effect. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/managing-microfrontends/vercel-toolbar#routing-overrides.

localProxyPort.description: The port number used by the local proxy server. The default value is 3024. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.

version.description: The version of the microfrontends config schema.
